description: My name is Sukaina Ahmed Alshaqqaq. I am passionate about physics, space, astronomy, and creative writing, with strong skills in leadership and collaboration. Why should you join my team? Simply put, together we will experience a unique, engaging, and hands-on scientific journey with far-reaching future impacts.
summary: Orbit of Echoes is an interactive, pixel-art space adventure created by a six-member Bahrain team for the NASA International Space Apps Challenge. Inspired by the idea that every abandoned vessel still has a story to tell, it turns forgotten spacecraft into a playable museum experience that blends exploration, learning, and fun. Players pass through three colored gates into distinct worlds. On the Moon, they explore the Apollo 11 site, the Lunar Rover, and a working laser reflector while hunting for four hidden tools. On Mars, they meet Spirit, Opportunity, Viking 1, and Perseverance, uncover clues about the planet's watery past, and attempt the "Seven Minutes of Terror" landing mini-game. In deep space, they visit the Voyagers and the Golden Record, managing dwindling power to keep the transmitter alive until 2040. Throughout, players collect story cards under the theme of lonely messengers carrying humanity's voice outward.
details:
What it does and how it works
Orbit of Echoes is an interactive pixel-art journey through three worlds: the Moon, Mars, and Deep Space. Players step through colored gates into open-air "museums" of abandoned or aging spacecraft, including the Apollo 11 site, the Lunar Rover, Spirit, Opportunity, Viking 1, Perseverance, and the Voyagers. They explore each site, find hidden objects, and collect story cards that tell each machine's story in its own voice. Each world has a challenge: finding four abandoned tools on the Moon, landing Perseverance in the "Seven Minutes of Terror" mini-game on Mars, and managing Voyager's fading power to keep its transmitter alive until 2040.

Benefits
It makes space history engaging and memorable instead of a list of facts. Players learn real mission details, such as Opportunity lasting almost 15 years when it was built for 90 Martian days, through play. It suits students and curious people of any age.

Intended impact
We want people to see spacecraft as explorers with stories, not just machines, and to feel curiosity about space exploration. All content comes from NASA mission pages, so the experience is also a trustworthy way to learn.


Tools and technology

  • Claude AI: helped us develop the story content, write the story cards and mission text, and shape the mini-game rules, such as the Voyager power budget and the Mars landing settings.
  • NASA libraries: we used NASA's mission pages and media library for the facts, dates, and figures, and for the real mission imagery in the slides. Our sources are listed in the deck (Apollo 11, Spirit, Opportunity, Viking, Perseverance, Voyager 1 and 2, and the Golden Record).

Creativity
The idea gives forgotten spacecraft a voice. The retro pixel style, gate-to-gate structure, and the theme "lonely messengers, still flying, fading, and carrying humanity's voice outward" tie three very different worlds together. Learning is built into the gameplay itself, such as setting real heat shield, parachute, and altitude values, or balancing Voyager's power budget in watts.

Factors we considered

  • Accuracy: facts drawn from NASA sources
  • Engagement: a mix of exploration, mini-games, and rewards (story cards, a bonus card)
  • Realism: mini-games based on real constraints, such as Voyager's 4 W yearly power loss
  • Emotion: a consistent theme so players connect with the machines
  • Inclusivity: the Golden Record's greetings include Arabic
